steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Vector graphics (Illustrator) use mathematical paths — they scale infinitely without quality loss; ideal for logos and illustrations.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Raster images (Photoshop) are pixel-based — they lose quality when enlarged; ideal for photo editing and digital painting.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Resolution matters: 72ppi for screen, 300ppi for print; RGB colour mode for screen, CMYK for print.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Layers, masks and non-destructive editing allow you to experiment without permanently altering your original image.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring digital design tools and techniques. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with digital design tools and techniques. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with digital design tools and techniques. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to digital design tools and techniques, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refi | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
